A.step_convention: t starts at 1 for the first gradient. Moments are initialized to 0. The parameter update is w_t = w_{t-1} + delta_w_t with delta_w_t = -lr * m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps) when bias correction is on.
A.epsilon_placement: Default matches PyTorch: epsilon is added after the bias-corrected second-moment square root, not inside it.

B.relative_difference_definition: rel_diff(t) = |delta_uncorrected(t) - delta_corrected(t)| / max(|delta_corrected(t)|, eps_rel). If the corrected update is smaller than eps_rel the denominator is clamped and the row is flagged.

constant.note: The persistent-tolerance crossing is searched up to search_limit and is reported separately from the 20-step plot.

varying.note: The persistent-tolerance crossing is searched up to search_limit and is reported separately from the 20-step plot.

C.near_zero_policy: ratio = ||delta|| / max(||w_before||, ratio_eps). Tensors whose *initial* ||w|| is below near_zero_weight_eps (zero-init biases) stay flagged for the whole run and are excluded from the headline mean; otherwise a tiny bias that moved on step 1 would dominate later ratios. Missing gradients are excluded. Non-finite values raise.
C.explanation: The schedule reaches its peak at warmup_steps by construction. The observed update-to-weight ratio can level off earlier or later because Adam's effective step size also depends on the moment estimates and the shrinking residual, not only on the nominal LR.

D.limitations: Single seed, synthetic modular-increment sequences, tiny Transformer. Results are not a universal ranking of cosine vs WSD.

matched.optimizer: Adam, identical peak lr and weight decay

D.checkpoint_rationale: Step 200 is an early-stop snapshot on a 300-step schedule, not a finished cosine run. Cosine has already started decaying; WSD is still at the peak. A 200-step-designed pair is reported separately because the ranking can change with the planned horizon.

E.parameterization: standard (Kaiming hidden, 1/sqrt(fan_in) head, zero biases). Not μP.
E.evaluation_metric: validation MSE against a frozen width-64 teacher

extrapolation.method: OLS of log(best_lr) on log(width), plus inverse-width heuristic from the largest measured width
extrapolation.uncertainty: Only three measured widths. The exponent is sensitive to which grid point is called the minimum and to the training horizon. This is an SP observation, not a μP transfer result: we do not claim the optimum learning rate is width-invariant.

protocol.init: Kaiming normal hidden weights, N(0, 1/fan_in) head, zero biases
protocol.data: same teacher-generated tensors for every width and LR
